_README: Goldened two-layer shim gap inventory. See test/shim-surface.test.cjs for what
this is and why it is a reviewed MAP rather than a must-be-empty gate.
Regenerate with UPDATE_GOLDEN=1, and add a note below for anything new.
Measured against the EXTRACTED cli.cjs (~21MB), never the 255MB Bun binary.

_notes.intl: NOT a node builtin — libexec/node-shim/modules/intl.cjs backs the Intl GLOBAL, not a require()able module, so neither side can enumerate it by name. Allowed, not a gap.
_notes.Bun.SQL: FIXED (no longer a layer1 gap, kept as history). Was an ACTIVE DIVERGENCE: upstream guards it with `if (typeof Bun > "u") throw Error("claude gateway requires the native binary")`, TRUE under real node ("undefined" > "u") but FALSE under quaude because bun-shim defines a Bun global at all — so the guard was defeated and `new Bun.SQL(...)` produced a bare `Bun.SQL is not a constructor` instead. bun-shim.cjs now gives Bun.SQL a throwing constructor that hands back upstream's own message verbatim. Reachability: confirmed NOT on the -p/interactive routes — Bun.SQL is used only inside the `claude gateway --config <path>` subcommand (a separate commander-registered enterprise auth/telemetry server), the sole call site in the bundle. See test/bun-shim-sql-guard.test.cjs.
_notes.Bun.WebView: BENIGN, and a good example of the shape we want: guarded by `"WebView" in Bun`, correctly false under the shim, so the branch is skipped and the function returns false. Feature detection that works.
_notes.bun:jsc: BENIGN. One site: `try { let {heapStats} = await import("bun:jsc") ... } catch {}` for heap diagnostics. The rejection is caught, so a missing module degrades to no heap stats, matching any non-Bun host.
_notes.bun:sqlite: DRIFT, not a gap: bun-shim declares an interceptor for it in PROVIDES but bundle 2.1.218 never imports it. Harmless dead weight; listed so the declaration's drift stays visible instead of silently accumulating.
_notes.http.request / https.request / net.creat: DECLARED WALLS — the same ones test/node-shim-wall-tripwires.test.cjs alarms on, rediscovered here independently without being told they exist. That rediscovery is the main evidence this map works. They throw branded node-shim errors rather than failing silently.
_notes.crypto.*: The largest cluster (X509Certificate, createPrivateKey/PublicKey, createSign/createVerify, sign, pbkdf2/pbkdf2Sync, KeyObject). Unaudited. Plausibly the enterprise auth paths (Vertex/Bedrock, mTLS) rather than the -p / interactive routes we support, which would make them unreachable in practice — but nobody has checked, and RECIPE.md G4 already flags that auth path as unverified.
_notes.fs.fchmodSync / fs.fstat / fs.ReadStream: FIXED (no longer layer2 gaps, kept as history). Were fd-flavored variants of things the shim DOES provide by path (chmodSync, statSync, createReadStream) — same class as the FileHandle.chmod gap that broke Edit, which is precisely why this map exists. fchmodSync now tracks fd->path at fs.openSync/close and chmods that path (no fd-based fchmod primitive in the sync-fs patch, same strategy FileHandle.chmod already used); fstat routes through the existing fstatSync via cbWrap; ReadStream is now a real class fs.createReadStream() constructs, not a lookalike. See test/node-shim-fs-fd-variants.test.cjs.
_notes.child_process.fork / ChildProcess: fork() has no meaning under tjs (no node child bootstrap). If a reachable path ever forks, that is a design question, not a missing function.
_notes.stream.Duplex: reads only (6), no calls — likely instanceof / prototype checks. Low risk, but a false instanceof silently takes the else-branch.
_notes.v8.* / perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay: diagnostics and telemetry; absent means no stats, not broken behavior.
